name: Rhode Island Eats: Restaurants
subtitle: Clam Shacks, Wieners & More
description:
Rhode Island's restaurants, from hot wieners up the arm to clam cakes in Galilee.

Rhode Island Eats is a free guide to eating in Rhode Island: 6 hot wiener joints, 13 clam shacks, 7 Federal Hill Italian dining rooms, 26 frozen lemonade stands and creameries, 3 bakery pizza strip shops and 3 Portuguese kitchens we checked by hand, plus 2,828 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries in all 39 cities and towns, Block Island included. No account, no ads.

RHODE ISLAND GUIDES
• Hot Wieners: New York System joints, meat sauce, mustard, onions and celery salt.
• Clam Shacks & Stuffies: clam cakes, clear chowder, stuffies and fried seafood.
• Federal Hill Italian: dining rooms on and around Atwells Avenue.
• Bakery Pizza Strips and Portuguese Kitchens.
• Frozen Lemonade & Creameries: frozen lemonade stands and ice cream.
• James Beard Honors and Oldest Places.

FIND IT FAST
• Sort by distance, or browse the map by guide.
• Search by name, town, street or dish: "hot wieners", "clam cakes galilee", "atwells".
• Filter by town or cuisine, or hide chains.
• Save places, and find hand-checked places from iPhone search (Spotlight).

LIVE DETAILS FROM APPLE MAPS
Tap "Ratings, hours & photos" on any place to open Apple Maps' own place card, with current hours, photos, ratings and directions.

HOW THE LISTS ARE BUILT
Every guide place was checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source: a dated magazine guide or local news story, or the place's own site. The rest come from Overture Maps open data, kept by a reliability rule tested against the Department of Health's own license list. The department's reports carry no score or grade and aren't published as data, so each place links its own inspection search. Website links are checked too. Nothing is ranked by star ratings, and the app computes no grades. Newer restaurant data downloads from the Rhode Island Eats website when there is some.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your location, if you share it, only sorts lists on your device. Saved places stay on your device.

Places open and close, so check before you go. Spot a mistake? Email nick@eatsranked.com.

An independent app, not affiliated with any restaurant, chain or government agency (including the State of Rhode Island or the Rhode Island Department of Health), or with the James Beard Foundation. James Beard Foundation and James Beard Award are trademarks of the James Beard Foundation. Place data from Overture Maps Foundation (CDLA Permissive 2.0) and others; sources and licenses are on the About tab.

reviewNotes:
1. Purpose and audience: Rhode Island Eats is a free guide to restaurants in Rhode Island (the U.S. state). Its focus is the state's own food: hot wieners, clam shacks and stuffies, Federal Hill, pizza strips, Portuguese kitchens and frozen lemonade, 59 places checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source, plus the James Beard honorees. It also lists 2,828 restaurants, cafés and bars in all 39 cities and towns from open map data, checked against the Department of Health's license list. It is for residents and visitors deciding where to eat, with no ads, account or tracking.

2. How to use it (no login, no setup, no sample files needed):
- Home → Hot Wieners (or Clam Shacks & Stuffies, Federal Hill Italian, Bakery Pizza Strips, Portuguese Kitchens, Frozen Lemonade & Creameries, James Beard Honors, Oldest Places, Near Me) → tap any place.
- On a place, tap "Ratings, hours & photos" to open Apple Maps' own place card through MapKit. Directions, Call and Website are below it; further down, a link opens the Department of Health's inspection search in Safari.
- Search from the Home search box by name, town, street or dish ("hot wieners", "clam cakes galilee", "atwells").
- The Map tab shows each guide as pins. "My location" and the Nearest sort use location only if allowed, on the device.
- The heart saves a place on the device (Saved tab). The About tab lists the sources, licenses and the independence statement.
- On iPad, a sidebar replaces the tabs; a place opens in the right-hand column.
- Location: if you're outside Rhode Island (as App Review usually is), the map says so and stays on Rhode Island, and distance sorting still works from where you are.
- "RI Eats" is the Home Screen name of "Rhode Island Eats: Restaurants".

3. External services and data:
- Apple MapKit: maps, local search to find a place's Apple Maps listing, and Apple's place card for live hours, photos and ratings.
- Core Location: optional, on-device only, for distance sorting.
- Data updates: at most once a day, the app checks the Rhode Island Eats website (static files on GitHub Pages) for newer restaurant data and downloads it if there is some. The requests carry no identifiers or location.
- No backend, accounts, analytics, advertising, payments or AI services. The restaurant data is bundled in the app.
- Bundled data sources: Overture Maps Foundation open place data (CDLA Permissive 2.0 and others; license texts are in the app); James Beard Foundation honors (facts only); and our own research of public websites and local news. Inspection reports are not copied: each place links to the department's own public search.
- The website with the privacy policy and support page is static and hosted on GitHub Pages: https://nickstrom5.github.io/rhode-island-eats/

4. Regional differences: none. The content covers Rhode Island; the app is offered in the United States and works the same everywhere.

5. Regulated or protected material: the app is not in a regulated industry and includes no protected third-party material. The data is open-licensed or public record, with attribution and licenses on the About tab. Ratings, hours and photos are shown only inside Apple's own place card through MapKit; the app stores no ratings or reviews. The app shows no inspection results and computes no grades. Every website link was checked before release, and adult venues are excluded. The app is independent and not affiliated with any restaurant, agency or the James Beard Foundation.
